rich_narrative.summary: Irusa Waqf serves as a long-term financial engine for Islamic Relief USA, focusing on <cite id="1">building a pool of capital</cite> to ensure the sustainability of humanitarian efforts. Founded in <cite id="2">1993</cite>, the organization operates on a traditional Islamic endowment model, where principal investments are preserved to generate ongoing support for <cite id="3">emergency relief, food distribution, and orphan sponsorship</cite>. In FY2024, the organization reported <cite id="4">total revenue of $1,912,900</cite>, reflecting its role as a specialized funding vehicle rather than a high-volume direct service provider. While the organization maintains <cite id="5">exceptional financial stability</cite> with over 392.9 months of working capital, its current operational phase focuses more on asset accumulation than immediate program expenditure. This results in a neutral balance between its <cite id="6">strong historical track record</cite> and a lack of current data regarding program expense ratios. For donors, the value proposition lies in <cite id="7">long-term institutional resilience</cite> and the ability to support a wide geographic reach, including <cite id="8">Gaza, Yemen, and Afghanistan</cite>, through a permanent charitable fund.
